newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end higher, seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end higher, seen bullish.

text.p: Austrian bonds ended firmer on Tuesday, driven mainly by technical factors and traders predicted the market would remain bullish in the next days.
The Bund future remained above the important support level of 102.65 without yielding to pressure from weakness in the U.S. markets.
"The U.S. markets are key, and as long as nothing happens here, there is still room for gains in the German Bund future" said one trader.
Trade was dominated by a newly-announced issue of a 30-year bond for which demand was "not bad", according to traders. But they said profit-taking could set in.
The coupon of the 15 billion schilling bond was fixed at 6.25 percent and final yield at 6.455 percent.
* 10-year benchmark 5.625 pct bond maturing July 2007 up 25 bps at 100.25 to yield 5.59 (5.63) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.10/18 to yield 5.61/5.60 pct.
* Five-year 4.625 bond maturing May 2002 steady at 100.20 to yield 4.58 pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.15/23 to yield 4.59/57 percent.
* Austrian bond future down 23 bps at 110.01 on turnover of 370 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany down one at four bps, five-year spread down one at 19 bps.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.393 and overnight money at 3.13/3.38. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
